title: Yankees reportedly extend Matt Blake with three-year deal
author: Madison Pavich
text:
The man behind one of the best pitching corps in baseball is locked down for the near future.

The Yankees knew that there was one face of Aaron Boone’s coaching staff they could not risk getting away from them, and they made sure to handle it before his contract officially expired. Matt Blake, the team’s pitching coach since the 2020 season, has reportedly agreed to a three-year extension to remain with the team according to the New York Post’s Jon Heyman. Heyman’s colleague Joel Sherman had reported yesterday that the two sides were working on a new deal, and with his current deal set to expire at the conclusion of this year’s World Series the time was nearing to get this thing done.

Blake has transformed the Yankees’ pitching philosophy since entering the organization, having the reins handed to him to lead an analytical breakdown of their pitching staff that has led to significant success. This season Yankees pitchers had the best collective ERA in baseball with a 3.23 mark, ranked third with a 3.71 FIP, and collected the fifth most fWAR at 21.9. Any way you sliced it, their pitching was the MVP of the roster, and it was led by the presumptive Cy Young Award winner in Cam Schlitter. They were far from a one-man show though, for once having more starting pitching than the team knew what to do with despite dealing with a host of injuries, as Max Fried, Gerrit Cole, and Carlos Rodon all turned in fine seasons.

The biggest factor in Blake’s rise to the top of the organization has been his work with the lesser-known prospects and journeymen the team has cobbled together. Will Warren has turned into a dependable fifth starter that most teams would jump at the opportunity to slot into the middle of their rotation, and Ryan Weathers took a major leap this year when trusted with a role in the rotation after being acquired last offseason. Meanwhile, the bullpen has continued to take on unknowns and spit out gems, this year seeing Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick form an unstoppable bridge to closer David Bednar after both entered the year as relative afterthoughts. The team has gotten similar leaps from relievers in the past, like Clay Holmes and Luke Weaver who both served as the team’s closers in recent years, and reigned in enough of Fernando Cruz’s wildness to make him an effective middle inning reliever until a UCL tear ended his season. Brian Cashman gets a lot of credit for finding the pieces of this staff out of thin air, but Blake’s role in leading the “pitching lab” has been just as crucial in developing their talent.

Blake now sits as one of the few men on the coaching staff with a secure position within the organization. His side of the roster was unquestionable in their pursuit of title No. 28 this season, and overall has produced time and time again since Blake has arrived. The man above him doesn’t have that much security, with Boone entering the final year of his contract this season without an extension in front of him. The pitchers have bought into Blake’s direction wholeheartedly and the results have been plain to see — now the work begins on finding the next set of unheralded arms to transform.

title: Six Flags to reopen Goliath rollercoaster – but now with seatbelts after recent rider death
author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
text:
Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem fell from ride earlier this month, spurring amusement park to temporarily shut it down

Six Flags will install seatbelts on its Goliath rollercoaster in Georgia , after a rider plummeted to his death earlier this month.

Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old father and educator, was thrown from his seat on the Goliath, a coaster that plunges riders down 165ft, before a second drop of 180ft. On his way down, he collided with the ride’s other cars.

Georgia authorities have launched a probe into Kariem’s death. The gruesome fall prompted the park to temporarily close the Goliath and eight rides at five other parks.

“What happened has deeply affected all of us at Six Flags. Safety has always been fundamental to the experience we provide for our guests,” the theme park’s CEO, John Reilly, wrote on Friday.

Seatbelts will also be added to coasters with a similar restraint, he announced, although an exact list remains unclear. The Goliath features a lap bar that locks over a rider’s waist, a design from Bolliger & Mabillard.

The park has also commissioned an independent review of the safety procedures for all of its attractions.

“I know trust is earned through actions and not words,” Reilly said. “We will continue to communicate about our progress and hold ourselves accountable to our commitments to you.”

The Six Flags Over Georgia fatal incident comes as the theme park is being sued over alleged bodily harm from its X2 ride at Magic Mountain. A recent CNN investigation uncovered a long history of brain injuries and at least two deaths linked to the ride.

A group of past riders who say they sustained brain injuries on X2 has accused the park of having a defective coaster and negligence for allowing its continued operation, according to court documents.

Six Flags permanently shut down the embattled X2 coaster in September.

title: Hundreds of thousands march in France as protests take place across Europe – Europe live
author: Patrick Daly(now);Marina Dunbar , Frances Mao and Emily Mackay (earlier)
text:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of events in Europe – we will be closely following protests across the continent today.

In France , hundreds of thousands are expected at rallies across the country, with high school students, unionists, “yellow vest” demonstrators and others turning out for a fourth weekend of protests demanding more government funding for schools and measures to help with housing and the cost of living.

Desperate to avoid the looting and property damage seen on the fringes of some protests last weekend, French authorities have ramped up restrictions on where protesters can march and which groups are “authorised” to do so. They’ve increased policing 20%, mobilising 70,000 police officers and soldiers to the streets, including both elite units and trainee officers.

Many of Paris’s metro stations and major museums and tourist sites are shut today, while across the country, shops and businesses have been urged to close their doors. Community tensions are also high following a deadly shooting on Friday west of Paris where the gunman targeted non-white people, killing one person and injuring five others including a child. The French president called it a “racist terrorist attack”.

Meanwhile, Marine Le Pen’s anti-immigration party is also due to hold its national conference in the central city of Orléans. The far-right National Rally’s meeting is expected to draw up to 30,000 counter-demonstrators. Protests are also being held in Italy, Spain, Austria, Portugal, Albania and Ireland today.

title: Hamilton leads final practice after Leclerc lap deletion
author: Matt Beer
text:
Ferrari completed a full set of top United States Grand Prix Formula 1 practice times in the final session at Austin, though a track limits deletion for Charles Leclerc meant this time it was Lewis Hamilton on top.

Friday pacesetter Leclerc lost a time that had been 0.083 seconds faster than Hamilton, falling to third behind Max Verstappen as a result as he had to rely on a medium-tyre time.

Ferrari had also been on top during the longer runs in the first part of the session before teams switched to qualifying simulations.

Hamilton expressed his frustration with Gabriel Bortoleto over a traffic incident - one of quite a few in the session - that will be looked at by the stewards.

Leclerc was far from the only driver to fall foul of track limits as the wild number of laptime deletions continued through the session. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli and both McLaren drivers were among the other high-profile transgressors.

Though Leclerc's lap loss meant Red Bull ended the session second with Verstappen, both he and Isack Hadjar had plenty of complaints over team radio and Verstappen having a wild lock-up, slide and wheelspin moment to end his session.

Alex Albon also received Hadjar's team radio ire - albeit for an 'impeding' incident that looked like it only happened because a big mistake from Hadjar carried him towards the slower-moving Williams.

Antonelli ended up fourth ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

The laptime deletions helped Nico Hulkenberg to get Audi as high as seventh, splitting the McLarens.

title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
author: Terrence O’Brien
text:
Pennsylvania’s AI Deceptive Advertising Act leaves a lot of loopholes.

Pennsylvania’s AI Deceptive Advertising Act leaves a lot of loopholes.

On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad — whether it’s a still image, video, audio, or text — that “has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence” to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants’ ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials.

Pennsylvania is one of the first states to require disclosures on AI content. And it requires those labels regardless of where an ad was created. So you might see disclosures pop up in commercials in other states if they’re also expected to air in Pennsylvania.

The law leaves many loopholes, though. For one, what constitutes “significantly modified” is subjective. There is also a carve-out for “parody, satire, commentary or criticism,” as well as anything that is “evidently fictional.” Again, what “evidently fictional” means is unclear. The wording also suggests only content that “uses synthetic content in a manner that creates a false consumer perception” about a product or service would require a disclosure. Again, leaving questions about what qualifies as “false” under the law and who makes those decisions.

The office of State Senator Nick Pisciottano, who introduced the bill , did not immediately return a request for comment.

title: Herta could replace Bottas at Cadillac in F1 2027
author: Josh Suttill
text:
Cadillac's 2027 Formula 1 driver line-up isn't yet finalised, with reserve driver Colton Herta among those in contention to replace Valtteri Bottas.

Both Bottas and Sergio Perez joined F1's 2026 new team Cadillac on long-term deals, but The Race understands the team hasn't made a final decision on who will drive for it next year.

In the Austin press conference on Friday, Cadillac team boss Marcin Budkowski left the door open when asked if Perez and Bottas will stay on for 2027.

"This is the last place I would comment on driver contracts, and in general, I think it's not something that is done in the press," Budkowski said.

"It's something which will be done by official releases from the team when the time is right."

Cadillac has to decide between sticking with the continuity of its two experienced drivers with knowledge of championship-winning teams or whether it's the right time to make a change with potentially bigger upsides for the future.

There's nothing to suggest Perez is at risk of losing his seat, as he's been the stronger Cadillac driver this year and has pushed the team hard behind-the-scenes to improve.

Bottas and Perez have been fairly evenly matched in qualifying this year, with Perez leading Bottas 13-9, but it's in the races where Perez has had a clear margin. Bottas has only spent 18% of the racing laps they've both been on track ahead of Perez.

Bottas has also had some particularly tough grands prix, including the last race in Singapore, where he was lapping around 1.5 seconds slower than Perez without a clear explanation.

That means his seat is in doubt for 2027, with 26-year-old Herta among those who could replace him.

Why "disappointing" F2 season hasn't hurt Herta's chances

Herta has had a self-described "disappointing" F2 campaign as he's 19th out of 22 full-time drivers with two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remaining.

"Maybe a few more questions than answers for me, maybe more questions than going into it, so I'm fairly disappointed with everything on that side of things," Herta said at Austin.

"I'm just disappointed with how the year's gone; it's not been good at all."

It's unlikely Herta will stay in F2 for a second season next year, but he's made it clear he'd still like a racing programme of some kind next year, with F1 still the ultimate goal.

Cadillac isn't put off by Herta's disappointing F2 performances as it knew making the switch would be difficult, and it's been impressed by the work Herta has done in its F1 car.

It does mean, however, that Herta's championship finish is all but certain not to earn him any superlicence points from F2, but Cadillac is ensuring he'll reach the 40-point threshold.

Herta took part in his fourth FP1 of the year at Austin on Friday, but only three of those are eligible for the superlicence bonus point, as a technical issue at Monza meant he didn't clear the 100km of running necessary to gain the superlicence point.

That, added together with his IndyCar results - including 30 points for finishing runner-up to champion Alex Palou in 2024 - means he's now one point away from the threshold.

The Race understands Herta will do another FP1 before the end of the year to make sure he gets to 40 points so he can be an option for 2027.

Herta has also completed private F1 testing away from the circuit, having run in an Alpine as part of that team's Testing of Previous Cars programme at Portimao, where he ran in a ground effect-era car.

Cadillac doesn't have a TPC programme of its own, so, just as when it ran Perez in an old Ferrari in late 2025, it's struck a deal with a rival team to ensure Herta gets more mileage.

Since first gunning for an F1 entry under the Andretti banner, Cadillac has long stated its ambition to have an American driver if one can earn a seat on merit with Herta the most logical candidate.

Herta isn't the only contender for Bottas's seat, as multiple drivers have been contacting Cadillac - it's the only ‘open' seat, with Racing Bulls only picking between Red Bull-contracted drivers.

Esteban Ocon is looking for a way to stay on the F1 grid next year after losing his seat to Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, but The Race understands he won't be joining Cadillac in a race or reserve driver role.

Instead, he's likely to take a reserve driver role at a different team such as Aston Martin.

Red Bull reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda is looking for a permanent return to the grid after his unexpected three-race return with Racing Bulls earlier this year.

Tsunoda's representatives have been contacting Cadillac over a 2027 opportunity and he is among the contenders.

Cadillac isn't in a rush to make a final decision, as none of the candidates have race seat options elsewhere.

Should it elect to replace Bottas for 2027, it would need to come to some kind of arrangement given he has a long-term deal with the team.

title: Tens of thousands of Lula supporters rally on eve of Brazilian election runoff
author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro and Tiago Rogero in Belo Horizonte
text:
Nearly 159 million people to head to polls on Sunday in battle between leftwing incumbent and Flávio Bolsonaro

Tens of thousands of supporters of Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, have streamed on to Rio’s most famous beach for a giant protest they hope will propel him towards a historic election fightback against his far-right rival, Flávio Bolsonaro .

Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election’s runoff on Sunday, with the pair tied in the polls after Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October by 47% to 45%.

On Saturday, under a fierce sun, red-clad crowds packed the 2.5-mile Copacabana beach in an attempt to help Lula clinch a dramatic and unprecedented comeback . Never since the return of democracy to Brazil in the 1980s has the first-round loser managed to bounce back.

Josias Silva, a 61-year-old truck driver, voiced confidence that his 80-year-old president would win a fourth non-consecutive term. He carried a homemade sign to the carnival-like procession reading: “Lula re-elected. Tomorrow will be a new day.”

“The people have woken up,” Silva said of the large pro-Lula street protests that have swept Brazil since the leftist’s first-round defeat, many led by students.

“Young people know we need this victory because otherwise we will have dictatorship again – and we don’t want dictatorship. We don’t want hatred. We don’t want guns. We want a country of love,” added Silva, celebrating the large number of people who came to witness one of the final presidential campaign rallies in Lula’s storied 50-year political career.

“There’s never been a demonstration like this one. This is the biggest protest in the history of Brazil. And we are going to win tomorrow with more than 60% of the votes,” Silva claimed.

Polls suggest a far tighter margin and most analysts see Bolsonaro, whose father, Jair Bolsonaro, was president from 2019 to 2022 , as the slight favourite, having sold himself to voters as someone who will tackle chronic levels of violent crime with an iron fist.

However, in recent days Lula has appeared to regain the initiative and climb in the polls, amid a succession of scandals involving his rightwing foe. Last week the Brazilian magazine Piauí claimed that at the height of Brazil’s 2020 coronavirus outbreak, Flávio Bolsonaro attended a boat party attended by sex workers and vaccine lobbyists hoping to strike a deal with the government of his father.

Some experts speculate a Lula comeback may be possible. At the Copacabana rally, activists unfurled an enormous yellow and green banner declaring: “WE ARE GOING TO TURN THIS AROUND!”

“I’m super excited. Lula’s going to win,” said Marta Moraes, a 59-year-old restaurateur, as she joined Saturday’s demo.

Moraes said the election was not about left versus right. “We’ve nothing against the right … what we’re against is Bolsonarismo,” she said, tears filling her eyes as she recalled how Flávio Bolsonaro’s father botched the response to Covid during his chaotic 2019-2022 administration.

“I lost four members of my family because of Bolsonaro’s neglect,” Moraes said.

Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after he lost the 2022 election to Lula. Many Brazilian democrats fear he will be released – and could even return to government – if his son wins. Reports in the Brazilian press suggest several of Bolsonaro’s fellow plotters – who are now in prison or hiding in exile – may be given top military and police jobs in a Bolsonaro administration.

Cammy Marinho, a 49-year-old DJ and activist, said: “I’m here to prevent democracy becoming extinct – which is what the Bolsonaro family wants”.

Marinho said she had spent the past fortnight fighting to persuade people who voted for Bolsonaro, or did not vote in the first round, to back Lula.

“It’s non-stop work: in the bakery, in the supermarket, on the underground – whenever you feel there is an opening to talk to someone and show to them the reality, everything that Lula has done and is doing for the people and everything that this [Bolsonaro] family has done against the people,” she said.

Many marchers were part of the so-called “Lula’s Army” – a 10 million-member WhatsApp group that was created after the first round in the hope of turning the election around.

“Being a soldier in Lula’s army … means fighting for Brazilian democracy. This isn’t a normal election,” said Isabella Gaze, 64, a retired teacher and one of the group’s members.

“They constantly claim Lula is corrupt. But the truth is that they represent the most rotten and worst part of Brazilian politics. This is what we are fighting against now,” Gaze said of the Bolsonaros.

Many of the faces on Copacabana beach were teenagers, including 14-year-old Heitor Lopes da Silva. Silva had come from the city of Duque de Caxias in his wheelchair, with a placard that said: “Lula, I’m a person with a disability and I’m here to support you.”

“My whole life I’ve believed Lula was a good president. [Bolsonaro] represents the destruction of Brazil …. he represents sadness and death,” he said of the Bolsonaro-era Covid catastrophe.

Large crowds of Bolsonaro supporters also hit the streets, including in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais state, which has Brazil’s second-largest electorate after São Paulo, and is a key bellwether. No presidential candidate has ever won the presidency without securing Minas Gerais, where Bolsonaro led by just under 5% in the first round.

Thousands of Bolsonaristas gathered to see their candidate in a palm-lined plaza called Praça da Liberdade. To the booming sound of AI-generated funk carioca tracks praising Bolsonaro, a sea of supporters dressed in Brazil’s yellow football jersey waved Brazilian flags – and many of the United States too.

“The US is a great nation. Who wouldn’t want to be aligned with them?” said 56-year-old cosmetics entrepreneur Marcos Antonio, holding a flag that merged the emblems of both countries.…

title: Manhunt under way to find prisoner who absconded from medical facility
author: Patrick Daly and Press Association
text:
Met police say Anthony Lloyd, 38, was last seen on Friday in south London, and ‘poses a risk to himself and the public’

A manhunt is under way to locate a prisoner who police say “poses a risk both to himself and the public” after he absconded from a medical facility in London .

Anthony Lloyd forced his way out of a health unit in Lewisham, in south-east London, shortly after 4pm on Friday, the Metropolitan police said.

The force warned the public not to approach Lloyd, but instead to contact 999 if he is spotted.

Lloyd was seen heading in the direction of Catford, police said in a statement on Saturday.

Lloyd was convicted in 2025 of actual bodily harm, according to the Press Association, relating to an incident in Nottinghamshire involving three emergency services workers.

He received a 12-month custodial sentence and was sent to prison . In September he was transferred to the medical facility in Lewisham.

The 38-year-old is white and about 5ft 8in, of medium build with short dark hair.

He was wearing a grey-blue T-shirt, black tracksuit bottoms and white trainers when last seen at about 4.10pm on Friday, police said.

Det supt Melanie Pressley, who is leading the manhunt, said: “We are conducting various significant inquiries to find Lloyd and return him to custody.

“We are concerned he poses a risk both to himself and the public, and would urge anyone who sees him to call 999 immediately. Do not approach him.

“If you have any information – however small – that could help us locate Lloyd, please get in touch with police as a matter of urgency.”

Officers believe Lloyd could be anywhere in the capital. He also has links to Surrey, Sussex, Thames Valley, Hampshire, Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire and Merseyside.

Anyone with information is asked to call 999, quoting the reference CAD4739/23Oct.

﻿Where does the Yankees payroll stand heading into the offseason?

The 2026 World Series matchup between the Tampa Bay Rays ( boo! ) and the Milwaukee Brewers ( yay! ) kicked off last night, and that can only mean one thing: the season is officially almost at a close. There are at most six games remaining, and baseball will be over after Halloween. Pretty soon, the stadium lights will dim, the locker rooms will go quite, and the hot stove will slowly begin to heat up as the winter begins.

The next few months will be even more hectic than usual. Not only will we be discussing potential free agent and trade targets, as we try to project how the Yankees might look to improve their squad for next season, we will also be following along the CBA negotiations, as Rob Manfred and the league owners attempt to engage in some ol’ fashioned robber baron-esque union busting. In order to prepare for these discussions — and to give you some good, hard data to cite when arguing with your friends — let’s take a look at where the Yankees’ payroll stands today.

Note: All guaranteed contracts are taken from Spotrac , and all arbitration estimates are taken from MLB Trade Rumors ; as always, given how much more focus the Yankees seem to place on luxury tax values than how much money is actually paid out in a given year, all numbers are based on their luxury tax hit.

The Yankees currently have seven players, including three-fifths of the starting rotation, under contract for the 2027 season, with a combined luxury tax hit of $212.4 million — more than the entire payrolls of 19 teams. Despite the large number, though, the Yankees are actually in fairly decent shape financially, at least in terms of the old rules: only three players (Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger, and Max Fried) are under contract past the 2028 season, and the players who provide the least value relative to their salary (Giancarlo Stanton and Ryan McMahon) have only one year remaining. Furthermore, because of Cody Bellinger’s opt-out (represented by the asterisks), his luxury tax hit for this upcoming season is substantially higher than it will be for the final four years of the deal—assuming he does not opt out, that is—due to the way Major League Baseball calculates these things.

As a rather fun aside, with Aaron Hicks and DJ LeMahieu finally off the books, the Yankees enter this winter with no dead money for the first time in years; it is presently unclear just how long this will remain true. Indeed, Stanton and McMahon stand out as potential options for dead money in 2027 should the Yankees decide that they’d rather eat their contracts than guarantee them roster spots.

MLB Trade Rumors projects the Yankees to have nine players eligible for arbitration this winter, with projected salaries ranging from $2.3 to $11 million. While we don’t yet know for sure whether the Yankees will actually tender contracts to all nine of these players — Fernando Cruz’s elbow injury and Luis Gil’s struggles (as well as his own injury history) make them likely candidates for release, while the high salaries relative to their health/production of Anthony Volpe, José Caballero, Heliot Ramos, and Clarke Schmidt might put them in at least mild jeopardy as well.

Technically, with no CBA signed, we do not know what the minimum salary will be for the 2027 season. We do have an upper and lower bound, though. Major League Baseball’s proposal from June pitched a minimum salary of $1 million, and MLBPA’s proposal from May advocated for a $1.5 million minimum. As such, although we don’t have concrete figures, we can nonetheless get a ballpark estimate as to how much the pre-arbitration salaries will cost.

As with the arbitration-eligible players, there’s a good chance that not everybody on this list will be tendered a contract. Punchless backup catcher Ali Sánchez and relievers Bradley Hanner, Kervin Castro, and Brendan Beck are just four players off the top of my head who should definitely not sign a one-year lease in the New York metropolitan area, at least until the non-tender deadline has passed.

As things currently stand, the Yankees 2027 luxury tax payroll sits somewhere between $265.1 and $273.1 million, or roughly $40 to $50 million below the Yankees’ 2026 payroll of $313 million (note: I removed player benefits and other non-payroll factors from the luxury tax equation, for the sake of consistency). While it remains to be seen how the CBA shakes out, and what the exact financial rules will be going forward, this gives us a rough estimate as to how much money the Yankees currently have at their disposal even if they aren’t looking to add to increase the team payroll in 2027.

title: Hundreds of thousands march across France in protests over schools and policing
author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
text:
Government estimates at least 400,000 people took part, but trade unions say the number is double that

Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful protests to support schoolchildren’s demands for more teachers and repairs to dilapidated buildings, as Emmanuel Macron faces a social and political crisis in his final months as president.

In Paris, at least 110,000 people marched along the eastern edge of the city, according to government estimates. They supported high schoolers but also complained of the high cost of living and the government’s heavy policing, saying riot police had been sent to target school protesters over the past month, instead of the government offering political solutions.

The mood in Paris on Saturday afternoon was peaceful and lighthearted, with brass bands playing and children and grandchildren present. Some people carried banners critical of the government’s policing, saying: “Oppression breeds rebellion” and “The right to protest”.

But at the end of the Paris demonstration, at Porte de Vincennes on the city’s eastern edge, different groups of masked men dressed in black emerged who had not appeared to have taken part in the peaceful march. Some groups of masked men threw glass bottles and stones at police, who responded with teargas, water cannon and stun grenades. A bin was set alight and fireworks were set off towards police.

Police also fired teargas to prevent protesters in Lyon, Lille, Montpellier, Nantes and Toulouse from reaching city centres. In Marseille, some bin fires were lit amid clashes with police.

The government estimated that at least 400,000 people had marched across France . Trade unions estimated the number at double that. The interior ministry said there had been almost 1,000 arrests.

More than 70,000 police were on the streets of French cities, with shops boarded up and many museums closed. The government had feared a repeat of last Saturday, when, despite peaceful protests taking place, France saw one of the most violent days of unrest in years with public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted and at least 2,700 people arrested in cities across the country.

At Saturday’s protests, there was widespread anger at Macron for banning non-union demonstrations that his government deemed “illegitimate” and for keeping all protesters away from city centres.

At the Paris march, Nadège, a 43-year-old communications worker, said she had been teargassed last weekend at a peaceful demonstration. “I’m out again peacefully today to support everyone who is brave enough to demonstrate. It does take courage. People are afraid now. We have to keep our rights alive … In France, it’s our legal right to protest in the street and I’m here to defend that.”

A 21-year-old student from a Paris science faculty that is now blockaded by demonstrators said: “We feel in France that we are increasingly living in an authoritarian regime that is trying to stop our democratic right to protest in the street.”

The government has been facing a crisis since the start of high school demonstrations in mid-September, when children aged between 15 and 18 began protesting against staff shortages at their schools, leaking and crumbling buildings, and a lack of chairs in overcrowded classrooms. It grew into the biggest youth movement in years, with trade unions, teachers and parents joining. Police investigations are under way after some children and protesters were maimed and injured by explosive police weaponry.

At Saturday’s march there were some people dressed in yellow vests who had taken part in the gilets jaunes anti-government protests of 2018 and 2019. Standing amid demonstrators, Jérôme Rodrigues, a key figure from the gilets jaunes protest, said: “Today the government is afraid; that is why they are pushing demonstrators to the edge of the city, away from places of power. It’s not police shields that will provide an answer to French people struggling and unable to make ends meet.” He said it was likely that demonstrations would continue each weekend.

Pierre, 60, a retired banking consultant, said he was demonstrating in support of school students. “I have an eight-year-old granddaughter. I want her to have a brighter future than the sombre times we are facing today. There is a complete refusal by the government to listen to people’s demands.”

Jesse, 40, a charity worker from the north of Paris, carrying a sign saying “Free Hugs”, said: “I’m so angry. I’m here to support schoolchildren’s demands for better conditions. I’m so proud of them and we have to stand together.”

She said: “I know I’m not going to war by coming out to demonstrate peacefully. But at times it really does feel like a war … This is the first time I’ve prepared so carefully for a peaceful march, wearing old clothes in case they are gassed or torn.”

In Orléans, thousands of people shouting anti-fascist slogans marched against a congress being held by Marine Le Pen’s far-right anti-immigration the National Rally party. Protesters criticised Le Pen, who is a frontrunner in next year’s presidential election, as well as Macron, who steps down from power next year. “Macron, resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd shouted.

title: Why Flying With a Bike is Always a Gamble (And How to Improve Your Odds)
author: Josh Ross
text:
If you buy through our links, we may earn an affiliate commission. This supports our mission to get more people active and outside. Learn about Outside Online's affiliate link policy

I travel with a bike more than most people, and it terrifies me every single time. After having a Look 795 Blade RS arrive broken in a Scicon AeroComfort case, I went down a deep rabbit hole—talking to the TSA and picking apart the fine print of airline contracts of carriage. Since then, I’ve learned even more by talking to the people who actually design bike luggage. Despite still being absolutely terrified of landing with a broken bike, I’ve learned a lot of info that rarely gets talked about. Here’s what I know about flying with a bike right now.

When you check baggage on a flight, you are agreeing to a contract of carriage. You might occasionally have to explicitly sign a waiver, but typically, you’ll hear nothing about it. You’ve still agreed to it, and if something happens to your bike, you are bound by those terms.

This contract outlines the liability an airline accepts when taking your property. Look carefully, because some airlines exclude bike liability completely, while others cap it at a specific amount that likely won’t cover a replacement frame. That cap drops even lower on international flights. The contract will also dictate what type of case is considered acceptable, and most airlines specify a hard case.

On top of airline rules, the TSA will almost always open your bag because it’s too large to be scanned. When I spoke to Sean Harbaugh, a supervisory TSA officer with 20 years of experience, he told me their biggest request is that cyclists stop packing extra gear and clothing into the case alongside the bike.

Add all of this up, and the reality is far less black and white than the airlines want you to believe—a gray area I’ll explain in a moment. But first, if your bike gets damaged, expect a huge fight to get a payout, and it will likely be less than you need. Regardless of the amount though, if you want any chance of succeeding, you must check your bike at the airport before you leave. You cannot make a claim once you walk out those doors. Open the case, check carefully for damage, and start the claim immediately if you find a problem. During that process, explicitly request that the security video of the TSA checking your bike be preserved. The inspection is always on video, but that footage will be overwritten unless you demand they pull it.

This is pretty obvious, and it’s what everyone thinks is the issue. Baggage handlers generally do not care about your bike. Sometimes they are outright hostile with it, but typically, they just don’t care. The bag will almost always get flipped on its side, and it will sometimes get slammed on the ground, a luggage cart, or a belt. Make sure whatever case you use will protect your bike from this treatment.

If your bars come off and you can fold them down, things are pretty easy. Even a cardboard box will typically work, although my favorite option for this scenario is the Topeak PakGo X. The real challenge comes when you are dealing with a modern bike and can’t take your bars off.

If that’s what you are up against, look for something that keeps your case from being crushed from the sides. The Orucase Sentinel is an incredible option that uses a rather genius internal aluminum roll cage. It protects the controls by running a rigid expansion bar through the drops that secures into place inside the case. I have a friend who actually uses the Scicon that broke my bike, but he uses PVC pipes to create an anti-crush system very similar to what Orucase is doing. Of course, a more traditional hard case will win out if you are only looking at what it takes to protect your bike from the baggage handlers.

After I had my bike broken, I swore I’d never fly with another soft case. Then I started using the Orucase Sentinel and had a conversation with the founder of Orucase, Isaac Howe. I’ve talked to him for years about the theory of bike cases, but recently we talked about what actually constitutes a “hard case.”

In talking to him, I realized I’d made a mistake in blindly believing the airlines. It seems like what the contract of carriage means is that you need a giant plastic or aluminum vault like a Shokbox or a Bike Box Alan. The reality is that no one has ever litigated it. If you have a soft outer material that covers a rigid internal structure, you can argue that it is still a hard case. Should someone go to court with that line of reasoning, they might well win. No one will actually go to court, though, so my advice is to think carefully about what you say if you ever make a claim. Your case could well qualify as a hard case, so don’t make the mistake of calling it a soft case.

The reason all of this matters is that you aren’t just protecting your bike from baggage handlers. If you were, a traditional hard case would be the undisputed answer. Instead, Howe told me that one of the hardest things to design for is the TSA. You meticulously pack your bike, everything is safe inside a hard outer shell, and then a TSA agent opens it and doesn’t bother putting it back together correctly. You might end up with a broken bike even though the case was strong enough to withstand anything a baggage handler could throw at it.

For my most recent trip, I ended up choosing the Post Carry Co. Loomer for this exact reason. It helped that Factor CEO Calvin Chan told me he carries the Factor ONE Bugatti edition bikes all over the world in that case, but it was also just the way it works. It’s essentially a hard case, but its simple closure system and the ease of seeing the bike made me think the TSA might be less apt to mess it up.…

title: Elisa Longo Borghini wins eighth Italian time trial title in Piasco
author: Lyne Lamoureux
text:
Elisa Longo Borghini wrapped up her season by claiming her eighth Italian individual time trial title in Piasco, following the postponement of the event originally scheduled for June. The UAE Team ADQ rider reclaimed the jersey after finishing runner-up to Vittoria Guazzini (FDJ United-Suez) in each of the past two years. Longo Borghini previously won the title in 2014, 2016, 2017, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023.

The 34-year-old rider averaged 50.839 km/h on the 19.7km flat and fast course, stopping the clock with a time of 23:15. Alessia Vigilia (Uno-X Mobility) took second, 54 seconds in arrears, while Letizia Borghesi (AG Insurance-Soudal) rounded out the podium.

The out-and-back route with 102 metres of climbing headed towards Costigliole Saluzzo before tackling two laps of a 6.7km circuit.

“I’m very happy to have won another Italian National Championship because I believe it’s a race that should always be honoured, even though this year it came at the end of a very long season," Longo Borghini said in a team release.

"It was a title I really wanted, because wearing the Italian champion’s jersey is always an honour. I’ll be happy to wear it next year in some of the biggest races on the WorldTour calendar."

The U23 title went to Giada Silo (UAE Development Team), who also claimed the Italian Road Race title in the Under-23 category back in June.

The Italian Cycling Federation postponed the junior, U23 and elite women’s time trial championships until late October, relocating the races to Piasco. The new date and location in the province of Cuneo were announced on October 8. The elite men’s event, won by Filippo Ganna (Netcompany Ineos), had gone ahead as scheduled in June in Barolo.

Guazzini did not defend her title, with just five riders lining up for the elite women’s time trial, down sharply from the 21 who contested last year’s event in June.

This season, Longo Borghini finished fourth in the ITT at both the World Championships and European Championships, and helped Italy win gold in the mixed relay at the Worlds. She also soloed to her seventh Italian road race title in June before finishing third at Tour de France Femmes and taking bronze in the road race at the World Championships.

title: Two More Teams Said to Be Interested in Roglič, Including a Major Wildcard
author: sstokes
text:
Primoż Roglič at the start of Il Lombardia (Photo: Silvia Colombo/NurPhoto) (Photo: Silvia Colombo)

The Slovenian had a spectacular return to form this autumn, winning the European time trial championships and taking secondo overall in the Vuelta a España.

At the same time there has been plenty of rumblings about his future plans, with the 36 hinting he wanted to continue while also saying that Il Lombardia could be the final race of his career.

It was hard to tell if the suggestion of retirement was due to potential dissatisfaction with what he had been offered, or simply a way of raising the stakes.

Indicating he was prepared to walk away was a message to anyone dithering that time was ticking and terms must be decided.

That race was two weeks ago and since then the possibilities have, apparently, continued to grow.

The latest? Two more teams are apparently interested in the rider, including one which was probably not on anyone’s radar but, for that squad at least, could make a lot of sense.

Unibet Rose Rockets is the latest to be linked to Roglič, with team founder Bas Tietema telling Sporza at the Tour de France presentation that he would potentially be of interest.

“There are also still a number of riders on the market without a contract, but we don’t want to make hasty decisions,” he said.

Asked if there had been any contact with Roglič, he confirmed both a historical link and a more recent one.

“A long time ago, we did get in touch with Primoz through our videos,” he said.

“And when he had a bad fall at the Vuelta, we also got in touch. He was really searching for direction then.

“I think he’d be great for almost any team. But we just need to see if Roglič is realistic for us. And I think he still has to decide if he even wants to continue riding.”

The squad is certainly of more modest stature than the others linked to the European champ.

Lotto-Intermarché, Tudor, XDS Astana, and Pinarello–Q36.5 are amongst those reported to have shown interest.

More recently his former team Visma-Lease a Bike has apparently been in touch, with Wielerflits reporting this week that several sources have confirmed talks between them.

Roglič spent eight full years with the team, finally leaving in 2023. His departure came after a Vuelta a España where he was forced to hold back and to allow teammate Sepp Kuss to win. He was a frustrated third, and headed to Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe seeking sole leadership.

That in turn disappeared when Florian Lipowitz finished third in the 2025 Tour, and when the team signed Remco Evenepoel.

Visma-Lease a Bike still has Jonas Vingegaard on board, meaning any decision to rejoin would see he and Roglič needing to share top billing.

However Vingegaard will likely target the Tour de France, potentially handing Roglič the number one slot in the Vuelta and, possibly, the Giro d’Italia too.

At this point in time Roglič shares the record of most Vuelta wins with four titles. Signing again with the Dutch team could see him have very strong backing for a fifth Vuelta success, an ambition that could well keep him in the sport.

Unibet Rose Rockets wouldn’t have anything like the same manpower to support such a goal. However it would eagerly offer him top billing if it helped get the nod for the Tour de France.

With perhaps just one more year left in his legs, Roglič may ultimately opt for whoever makes him the biggest offer.

Would the Rockets have the financial clout for that? The budget would certainly need to increase but, on the plus side, signing a rider as good as Roglič would boost their chances of a Tour invite.

Being passed over this year was a disappointment; having one or more big names on the roster would be the best way to sidestep that problem next year.

Financial offers aside, there is one other factor which could make all the difference.

Some riders’ families get cold feet about them spending a lot of time on the road. Jonas Vinegaard’s wife, for example, has complained about long absences from home, including at multiple training camps.

Vingegaard contemplated retirement over the issue but was able to get Visma-Lease a Bike to relax a little on its demands.

For Roglič, there seems to be a clearer understanding back home about what is needed.

“I think it’s not time to go home yet,” his wife Lora told Slovenian publication Sportal this month

“I’m not ready for this moment, especially since it is so sudden,” she said, becoming visibly emotional when discussing his possible retirement.

“I hope it’s not that… I really wish this isn’t the last time we talk about it or that I have to look back.”

Asked if she wanted to see him continue to race, she suggested he himself wanted to.

“He’s not ready to go home yet,” she said, then joked about taking up a lot of sport herself. “What are we going to do now? I can’t run marathons.

“I think he’s not ready to go home yet, but we have to respect the decision he will make.”

It sounds like she is fully committed if he decides to go on.

Finding a team which is similarly dedicated to the project is what is needed now, particularly as there are fresh indications that he too wants to keep racing.

That’s according to Spanish newspaper AS, which reports that there will ‘soon’ be news about his future, and what it terms a new destiny.

It also reports that he has ‘the desire to continue and several offers to choose from.’

With team building camps already taking place in various countries, plus the time to knuckle back down to training again fast approaching, a decision is indeed likely in the days or weeks ahead.

title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Hugh High
author: Nick Power
text:
Remembering a Yankees outfielder from the dawn of the franchise.

Before the Yankees were the Babe Ruth-led behemoth that took the baseball world by storm in the ‘20s, they were the laughingstock of the American League. Between 1913, their last year as the Highlanders, and 1914, their first as the Yankees, the team went 107-196. Things got bad enough that there were rumors the team might flip to the upstart Federal League, a nascent third major league that threatened the AL and NL.

Determined not to lose his New York franchise, AL president Ban Johnson worked behind the scenes during the 1914-15 offseason to strengthen the team’s roster, making it more attractive for a prospective new ownership group. He did so by encouraging the rest of the league’s teams to sell the Yankees useful players at a reasonable price. The first team to heed his call was the Tigers, who sold New York two players: a first-base prospect named Wally Pipp and a 27-year-old outfielder named Hugh High.

Hugh Jenkins High Born: October 24, 1887 (Pottstown, PA) Died: November 16, 1962 (St. Louis, MO) Yankees Tenure: 1915-18

High grew up in a family of 13 kids, three of whom would eventually play in the big leagues. The Highs were an itinerant bunch, living first in Pennsylvania, then New Jersey, then Illinois, and finally St. Louis in Hugh’s youth. He played semi-pro ball while serving as a plumber’s apprentice, making the jump to pro ball only after completing his obligation. He played well enough at Class-B Hartford of the Connecticut State League to draw the attention of several teams, including the Giants, who purchased his contract for $2,500 but ended up selling him back to Hartford for the same amount before he was able to join New York. High kept performing the next season and was once again a sought-after commodity, with the Tigers securing his services for the 1913 season.

High joined a crowded outfield picture in Detroit, with future Hall of Famers Ty Cobb and Sam Crawford as well as Bobby Veach, who’d finish a 14-year career with 2,063 hits and a .310 lifetime average. Still, he cracked the roster as a reserve outfielder and saw an expanded role early on with Cobb holding out due to a contract dispute and Veach on the shelf with an ankle injury. High played well enough that, when the roster returned to full strength, both Cobb and Crawford were briefly moved to the infield in separate stints to keep the rookie in the everyday lineup. While his raw stats never wowed, High was valued for his situational hitting and defense and developed a close relationship with the team’s manager, another future Hall of Famer named Hughie Jennings.

High improved in his second campaign, getting on base at a .363 clip while continuing to impress with his glove. The following offseason, the Tigers sold the talented youngster to New York to assuage Johnson’s concerns. His first season in pinstripes would be a career year. Finally given a full-time opportunity, he played in a career-high 119 games and showed some more pop, notching 27 extra-base hits after hitting 15 in the previous two years combined. High also swiped 22 bags, showcasing an all-around skill set that was an asset to a Yankees team still searching for an identity.

Prior to the start of the 1916 campaign, the Yankees continued to beef up their roster, headlined by the addition of future Hall of Famer Frank “Home Run” Baker. They put up their first winning season since their days as the Highlanders with High firmly entrenched in left, continuing to get on base consistently and play fundamentally sound baseball. He dealt with an ankle injury for much of the year, though, a harbinger for what was ahead.

The next offseason, High dealt with blood poisoning from an infected blister in his foot that set him back in spring training. He missed more time during the year as he dealt with boils on his neck. He ended up getting replaced in the lineup in September and would never regain his starting role. After the ‘17 season, the Yankees shopped High extensively, nearly reaching deals with the Senators, Dodgers, Red Sox, and Cardinals. They finally reached an accord with the Athletics a few weeks into the season but High refused to report to his new club. The Yankees suspended the outfielder and he walked away from the game, taking a job at a Maryland shipyard rather than shipping off to Philadelphia.

It was the start of an odyssey for High. The Red Sox tried again to trade for him; when High demanded back pay for the time he was suspended, the Yankees balked and he instead returned to the shipyard. The league reinstated High in 1919, but when the Yankees attempted to option him to the minors, he once again chose his job in Maryland. In May of that year, he finally accepted his sale, this time to the Vernon Tigers of the Double-A Pacific Coast League. High spent five seasons there, followed by another with Double-A Columbus and a final season with the International League’s Reading Keystones at the age of 37. Throughout this seven-year wilderness period, he showcased the consistent bat and slick fielding which had made him a valuable big leaguer in his youth.

After his baseball career, High returned to St. Louis, resuming the plumbing career he had put on hold in his early 20s. He died on November 16, 1962 at the age of 75. While never a star, Hugh High was a ballplayer’s ballplayer who helped shore up the Yankees franchise in its early, uncertain days and, through his long journey in minor-league baseball, demonstrated a love of the game few can match.

title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions
author: Donna Ferguson
text:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy offers thanks to US allies for restoring system key to air defence and ‘frontline logistics’

Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has said, 10 days after its ability to use the satellite communications system was suddenly restricted .

The Starlink satellite terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations. Sudden speed restrictions on the terminals, which capped operations at speeds of 160km/h (99mph), led to the failure of several Ukrainian combat missions earlier this month.

The military’s ability to intercept Russian attack drones was hampered and some Ukrainian operations to strike behind enemy frontlines were cancelled. Russia was able to launch ballistic missiles at Ukraine without any advance warning from the US.

The speed restrictions coincided with the announcement by Donald Trump of a US deal to buy Russian diesel , although the US president initially denied that his administration was behind the decision to cut intelligence sharing with Ukraine.

“I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” Trump said, referring to Musk, SpaceX’s chief executive.

However, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, appeared to throw suspicion on Musk when he defended Trump last Wednesday. “The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr Musk,” Rubio said. “That’s a private company. The president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything.”

Musk was quick to blame the limits on Starshield on the Trump administration , writing on X last week that the systems were “owned and controlled by the US government”. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately Potus [president of the United States],” he wrote.

The US vice-president, JD Vance, backed Musk on Thursday, saying the billionaire “doesn’t want to get in the middle of what is a war between two state actors without the United States government effectively directing him on what to do”.

Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , blamed both parties: “It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed … And technically, SpaceX did it.”

There were no similar restrictions on Starshield terminals in EU countries and that they applied only to Ukraine, he added. “In other words, this is a planned operation.”

He said the decision would “bring a lot of human losses … of course people would die”.

Announcing the restoration of the system on Saturday in a diplomatic video address on the Telegram app, Zelenskyy expressed his gratitude to his US allies, including Trump and the US state department, for resolving the operational issue: “The most important development for ‌today is that Starlink ‌and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the ‌level we need.”

The restoration began overnight. “By this morning, the speeds were already sufficient for operational use,” Zelenskyy said. “This is very important and significant for our frontline logistics and for defending Ukraine against jet-powered Shaheds.”

On Thursday, Trump had claimed the service was running again at full speed, but a European official speaking to the Associated Press denied the service was fully functioning.

When asked by reporters whether he would tell Musk to stop “messing around” with Ukraine’s access to Starlink on Friday, the US president said: “I’ve not spoken to him. I might have to … I’ve heard it was fixed. But if it’s not, I’ll speak to him … If there is a problem, I’ll get it straightened out.”

He then described Musk as a “very brilliant” and “very good” person.

title: Sam Fender tells fans high ticket prices for Proper Massive tour are ‘getting changed’
author: Priya Bharadia
text:
Fender criticises stadium pricing, calling it ‘bollocks’ and says it ‘won’t be happening’ on his tour

Sam Fender has responded to criticism by fans about ticket prices for his 2027 stadium tour by promising he would lower the cost, telling followers on Instagram: “They’re getting changed.”

The 32-year-old musician announced his Proper Massive stadium tour earlier this week.

Gavin Davis, an Instagram user, shared details of standing tickets for Fender’s show at Wembley, which were split into “front standing”, costing £130.75, and “standing”, priced at £98.85. Prices for seating ranged between £64.75 and £130.75.

Responding to the post, Fender said he was “not happy with these prices”.

He said: “It got inflated well more than I’d had in mind, it should only be inflated in relation to the cost of putting the show on.”

In his reply, Fender also criticised the division of standing tickets into front and back tiers as “bollocks”, saying this “won’t be happening” on his tour.

“I have no idea how this was normalised in gigs,” he added.

Tickets at other venues were also listed at more than £100, with the highest ticket price in Newcastle at £112.90, in Cardiff £119, and in Edinburgh at £120.95. The top ticket price in Manchester was £119.60.

Tickets for the tour are due to go on sale on Friday, with a presale on Wednesday morning.

Fender is not the first pop star to criticise ticket prices for his own show. The Swedish pop singer Zara Larsson has also called out steep ticket prices. In a TikTok post in August, she agreed with criticism from fans that ticket prices for her show in Bangkok were “very expensive” and wished to be “more involved” with setting prices.

“I hate the fact that people genuinely want to come, but they can’t because of the prices,” Larsson added.

Fender will perform at Newcastle’s St James’s Park, Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, Dublin’s Marley Park, Murrayfield in Edinburgh and the Etihad in Manchester across summer 2027.

Earlier this week, Fender also confirmed there would be a fourth album but he has yet to release the title or cover.

Fender, who was born in North Shields in Tyne and Wear, is best-known for his hit songs Hypersonic Missiles, Seventeen Going Under and People Watching. He is also the winner of five Brit awards and received the Mercury prize for his 2025 album People Watching.

Earlier this year, Fender rerecorded his single Rein Me In as a duet with the English singer-songwriter Olivia Dean, which won 2026 song of the year at the Brit awards. The song spent 23 overall weeks at No 1 in the singles chart, making it the longest-running No 1 single in British history.

title: Ferrari's last major 2026 F1 upgrade explained
author: Gary Anderson
text:
Ferrari has arrived in Austin with what should be its last Formula 1 car update of 2026.

From what we can see, it’s not a massive change - just small changes to the details in various areas, but as I often say, they all add up.

To be honest, Ferrari has not been that far behind as far as performance is concerned. It's been points lost through execution and decision-making. I know that Lewis Hamilton put his hand up as to not pitting under the VSC in Singapore, for instance, but that’s just one example of Ferrari's indecisions costing it.

Without doubt, Hamilton has lots of experience when it comes to making pit calls - some good, some bad - but my concern with the driver overruling the team is that for any driver, they only have their own information, and at most that of the cars in front and behind them, as to what the tyre situation is. The team has - or at least should have - the information from all of the cars still running, so a much broader picture of what is happening, so it should be able to make a better decision.

I say 'should' here because I have no idea if Ferrari looks any further than its own cars and also there seems to be a bit of a reluctance for anyone to put their heads above the parapet. If you don’t make decisions, you can never be held responsible for making the wrong decision.

Ferrari has also thrown away quite a few points by not allowing whatever driver is fastest to just press on - again, that falls into the reactiveness of decision making.

Anyway, that’s my moan for today - onto the developments. As I said, from what I can see, it is small detail changes.

The purple fin separating the radiator intake from the coke bottle undercut seems to have increased in size slightly. As the car speed increases, the radiator will not be able to flow the volume of air that is presented to it - when this happens, the inlet duct will start to spill around the outer body surface. This fin will reduce the adverse effect this spillage would have on the undercut sidepod.

In reality, it means that the floor foot vanes (bargeboards) will perform more consistently.

As for the sidepods, there's a change to the overall profile. The upper surface is now lower at the rear, inducing more downwash over that upper surface. This means that the sidepod's volume at its trailing edge has been reduced, opening up the coke bottle section between the inside of the rear brake duct and the inner body surface.

Also, the small undercut below the CEVA decal looks like it has also been increased in depth. These small changes in body profile reduce the amount of airflow that is presented to the outer edge of the underfloor - airflow in that area will be pulled under the underfloor by the low pressure underneath the car, and in turn that will reduce the overall downforce produced by the underfloor.

To go hand in hand with the changes at the sidepod inlet and the sidepod itself are novelties in the diffuser area. On the outer upper trailing edge corner, Ferrari has gone from a simple gurney flap (highlighted in green) to a more sophisticated vane (highlighted in purple). This outer corner is one area that can suffer from airflow separation problems. The new vane connects it to the multiple turning vanes mounted on the inner surface of the rear brake ducts.

Ferrari has also introduced changes to the diffuser vanes (highlighted in blue). There are probably further changes, but the obvious is the different trim to the lower trailing edge corner - this new detail should instigate a vortex, perhaps even two vortices, coming off that now-90° rear corner. If so, this will help seal that splitter to the track surface, improving the performance of the actual diffuser inboard of them.

Anything like this, when you are attempting to work the diffuser and underfloor harder, can very easily increase sensitivity to the track surface so lead to pointy downforce. However, in Austin, because of the bumpy track surface, Ferrari will probably be running the car just that little bit softer and, with that, a millimetre or two higher. The same is true for other teams that might be suffering from the same problems - so Mercedes might be able to get a better performance from its updates introduced in Malaysia (Bahrain).

Overall, it’s great to see at least four teams and eight drivers battling with each other, that’s what racing should be about - on top of that, as a small team, it is good to see Racing Bulls keeping those four big teams honest.

title: Northern Olympics campaign to get £7m in Healey’s budget
author: Sammy Gecsoyler
text:
Fund will support feasibility study for potential bid to host Games in 2040s, backed by northern mayors and top athletes

John Healey is to announce a £7m fund to examine a potential future bid to host the Olympics in northern England in his first budget as chancellor.

The fund will be used to carry out a full feasibility study for a northern Games, which, if successful, would be held in the north of England in the 2040s.

In May, before Andy Burnham entered No 10, the government commissioned an assessment by UK Sport which could inform a bid for the international sporting event in the 2040s. If the campaign were successful, it would be the first time the Olympic Games and Paralympics were hosted in Britain since London 2012.

There was further momentum behind the idea in June when mayors from across the north of England met in Sheffield to discuss the possibility of a northern Olympic bid.

More than 40 Olympians, Paralympians and elite athletes, including Laura Kenny, Jason Kenny, Sarah Storey, Beth Tweddle and Tom Pidcock, have signed a joint statement “to express our strong and united support” for the idea to hold a “box office Games” in the north of England.

Announcing the fund, Burnham said an Olympics bid would “unlock opportunity across our towns and cities” and that “we can put on the greatest show on Earth”.

He continued: “Few things bring a country together quite like the Olympics. I want people to feel that sense of excitement again, and to experience it in their own towns and communities, not just watch it on the telly.

“The Games would unlock opportunity across our towns and cities for the whole country. From north to south, it would be something everyone could get behind and be proud of.

“We know we can put on the greatest show on earth. Now we want to explore how we can do it again, with the whole country behind it.”

The full feasibility study will look in greater detail at how the Games would work in practice, including types of venues and transport links needed and the prospects of developing a winning bid. It will also look into how much it could cost and examine the chances of a bid succeeding.

The work will involve the government, UK Sport, the northern mayors and the British Olympic and Paralympic Associations, who would ultimately be responsible for a bid.

Healey said: “The north hosting an event as big as this would be truly unforgettable.

“Britain’s experience of London 2012 is proof we can host the world. I’m picking up the pace on our work to potentially bid for these prestigious Games.

“It will lift communities, create opportunities and give the UK a huge boost.”

The British Olympic Association, ParalympicsGB and UK Sport released a joint statement welcoming the news.

“Building on the success and legacy of London 2012, we look forward to working in partnership to explore this exciting opportunity and the benefits it could deliver for the nation, and for the global Olympic and Paralympic movements,” they said.

Sydney, Tokyo and London are among the mega-cities that have played host to the Olympics in recent years but Brisbane, Australia’s third-largest city, will be hosting the 2032 Games.

The Mayor of London Sadiq Khan has previously criticised plans to explore a bid to host the Olympics in northern England, saying that excluding London would be a “missed opportunity”.

title: Fielded is obsessed with scammers and unhinged Japanese cyberpunk
author: Terrence O’Brien
text:
Some Kind of Animal, the latest record from Fielded, jumps from slinky R&B, to neo-soul, to industrial funk.

Some Kind of Animal, the latest record from Fielded, jumps from slinky R&B, to neo-soul, to industrial funk.

Lindsay Powell, who releases records under the name Fielded, has spent most of her career subverting expectations and genre conventions. According to their Bandcamp page, Fielded started as an experimental noise project before growing into something closer to R&B. But from moment one, her take on the genre was restless, relentlessly playing with what R&B even means.

Her first album, Ninety-Thirty-Thirty , includes songs heavily indebted to ’80s synth-pop and features multiple saxophone solos. Boy Angel is a quirky electronic exploration with huge saw-wave synths, jittery percussion, and sky-high vocal stacks. While 2020’s Demisexual Lovelace is a slinkier affair, released on underground hip-hop imprint Backwoodz Studioz and features contributions from Billy Woods and Elucid (Armand Hammer).

Her latest record, Some Kind of Animal , pulls from all of these various versions of Fielded, placing organ-fueled slow jams like “That Bitch” next to a cover of Nine Inch Nails’ “Closer” that has strong 2000s neo-soul vibes, as well as the industrial funk of “Heaven,” which includes a guest verse from Pink Siifu.

We wanted to know what’s behind Fielded’s genre-defying madness.

My most indispensable tool in recording is my Universal Audio Apollo Twin audio interface. I love its ease of function and I love the Universal Audio digital studio plugins. I use them on all of my records during the recording process and beyond. I can mic up and get a professional sound in no time, plus my guitars and synths sound amazing and clear.

What sites do you have pinned to your tab bar?

Right now I have a pirated full-length version of the Japanese cyberpunk film 964 Pinocchio pinned to my tab bar for endless sonic and visual inspiration.

Which tech trend do you wish would go away?

I don’t know if it is a tech trend or a plague, but I deeply wish AI would disappear off of the face of the earth.

I am most proud of my latest album Some Kind of Animal , specifically the single of the same title, and thank goddess for that; I’d be bummed if my favorite musical output was in the rearview.

What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?

The best piece of advice I’ve ever received, throughout my whole life, is to be patient. Everything happens in perfect time; there is no reason to be jealous or envious because our journeys are completely our own and everything happens for a reason. What is meant for us will come for us, and what is not meant for us should be metabolized as a lesson that helps us grow and become exactly who we are meant to be.

I am currently obsessed with stories about scammers. All stories about all scammers; big scams, small scams, scams that ended in minor jail time or a blow-out of incredible impact. I love scammers, and I am fascinated by their brains.

title: HG Cross Heerderstrand: Joran Wyseure outpowers Joris Nieuwenhuis to claim first win of the season
author: Lyne Lamoureux
text:
Joran Wyseure (Crelan-Corendon) claimed his first win of the cyclo-cross season on the lake-side course at the HG Cross Heerderstrand in the Netherlands.

In a final-lap duel with defending champion Joris Nieuwenhuis (Heizomat-Cube), the Belgian used his power to full effect in the sand section, taking the longer line close to the water to find traction on the wet sand. The move gave him a few seconds of breathing room, which he steadily extended to seven seconds by the finish line.

Defending champion Niels Vandeputte (Alpecin-Premier Tech) took third, crossing the line, 16 seconds later ahead of Felipe Orts and 18-year-old Giel Lejeune (Alpecin-Premier Tech).

“It means a lot for me. I think every win is special, and it's a nice circuit here. I think it was a nice battle also with Joran and Niels, and I'm really happy I could make it off,” Wyseure said.

As the light changed quickly from red to green, riders on the left-hand side, including Wyseure, Orts, Laurens Sweeck (Crelan-Corendon) and Pim Ronhaart (Baloise Verzekeringer-Het Poetsbureau Lions), seemed not to be paying attention and had a slow start, and only Wyseure and Orts were able to recover to make it to the front of the race.

In the opening rounds of the nine-lap race. The front of the race shuffled and re-shuffled until six riders escaped at the end of the fourth lap, with Nieuwenhuis, Vandeputte, Orts, Mees Hendrikx (Bomba-Join), Lejeune and Wyseure making the front group.

With the sunny and slightly windy conditions drying out the course, riders were taking and testing the two different lines on the deep sand sections, with a shorter inside line and the more compacted sand on the outside, longer line.

At the end of the seventh lap, Wyseure powered to the front and applied pressure, with Hendrixx falling off the pace. He stayed at the front for the next lap, stretching out the group with his high pace until the elastic broke.

With one lap to go, Wyseure and Nieuwenhuis were locked in a duel until Wyseure broke away, giving a final look over his shoulder before speeding down the finishing straight.
